topic_summary: Division 7A benchmark interest rates for private company loans under the Income Tax Assessment Act 1936. The current rate for the 2027 income year (ended 30 June 2027) is 8.77%, the 2026 income year rate is 8.37%, and prior years range from 4.52% to 8.77%. Companies with a substituted accounting period must look up the Reserve Bank rate last published before their period start date — for example, 6.77% for a period starting 1 November 2022, and 8.02% for a period starting 1 May 2023. No competitor explains these rates with concrete year-by-year figures or addresses the 2026 legislative and administrative changes affecting complying-loan benchmark interest rates.

terminals.heading: What is the Division 7A benchmark interest rate for the 2027 income year?
terminals.result_copy: For a private company with an income year ending 30 June 2027, the Division 7A benchmark interest rate is indicated to be 8.77%. This rate is the 'Indicator Lending Rates – Bank variable housing loans interest rate' (Housing loans; Banks; Variable; Standard; Owner-occupier) last published by the Reserve Bank of Australia before the start of the 2027 income year. The rate does not change if the RBA later revises its published rate after the start of the income year.

terminals.heading: I'm not sure which benchmark interest rate applies to my company's substituted accounting period — how do I find out?
terminals.result_copy: If your private company has a substituted accounting period, the benchmark interest rate that applies is determined by identifying the 'Housing loans; Banks; Variable; Standard; Owner-occupier' rate last published by the Reserve Bank of Australia before the start of that company's income year. Because the applicable rate depends on the specific start date of the substituted accounting period, review of the RBA's published indicator lending rates for the relevant date is recommended to confirm which rate applies to your company's circumstances.

terminals.heading: How does the benchmark interest rate work if my private company has a substituted accounting period?
terminals.result_copy: For a private company with a substituted accounting period, the applicable Division 7A benchmark interest rate is the 'Housing loans; Banks; Variable; Standard; Owner-occupier' rate last published by the Reserve Bank of Australia before the start of that company's substituted accounting period — not the standard table rates. The verified figures show that a company whose substituted accounting period started on 1 November 2022 would use 6.77%, and a company whose period started on 1 May 2023 would use 8.02%. Review recommended to confirm the exact RBA rate last published before the start of your company's specific substituted accounting period.

terminals.heading: What happens if a Division 7A loan does not meet the benchmark interest rate requirement — what is a deemed dividend?
terminals.result_copy: The deemed-dividend consequence under Division 7A arises where a private company loan does not meet the required conditions, including the benchmark interest rate requirement. The applicable benchmark interest rate is the 'Indicator Lending Rates – Bank variable housing loans interest rate' (Housing loans; Banks; Variable; Standard; Owner-occupier) last published by the Reserve Bank of Australia before the start of the income year. Review recommended to assess whether the specific loan terms and interest charged meet the Division 7A requirements for the relevant income year.
